name: A Peon's Burden
summary: Ukor waits outside the Valley of Trials with provisions he cannot carry home. The recruits in the red canyon refused his food, so he asks travelers to take it back to Razor Hill.

sections.title: A Misplaced Delivery
sections.body: Ukor left Razor Hill carrying provisions for the fresh recruits training in the red canyon. He thought they needed the food, but the taskmasters sent him away. They keep rations meager, believing hardship teaches young Horde warriors discipline and endurance. Innkeeper Grosk later explains that hunger is part of their training.

sections.title: Perils of the Red Waste
sections.body:
Ukor reached the pass, but fears crossing Durotar on the way back. Scorpids, venomous spiders, and prowling boars haunt the rocky trail. He has no weapons or armor, and lacks the fighting spirit expected of an orcish grunt.

So Ukor waits along the path and asks travelers leaving the proving grounds to carry his heavy provisions back to the inn in Razor Hill.

aliases: who is the peon on the road
faq.answer: Ukor is a timid orc peon waiting on the road out of the Valley of Trials. He set out from Razor Hill with provisions, but fears the local wildlife too much to make the return journey alone.

faq.q: Why didn't the trainers in the Valley of Trials want the food?
faq.answer: The taskmasters keep the trainees hungry because they believe hardship teaches discipline and endurance. Innkeeper Grosk explains that meager rations are part of their training, so Ukor's provisions were refused.

faq.q: Where does this delivery need to go?
aliases: who do i give the food to
faq.answer: Carry the provisions north along Durotar's main thoroughfare to Razor Hill. Give them to Innkeeper Grosk inside the settlement's tavern.

faq.q: What makes the journey dangerous for a peon?
faq.answer: Scorpids, venomous crawler spiders, and wild boars roam Durotar's rocky wastes. Ukor is an unarmored, untrained laborer, while seasoned recruits can handle such vermin.

faq.q: What is the role of peons in the Horde?
faq.answer: Peons hold the lowest place in orcish society and do menial work, from hauling supplies and chopping timber to raising fortifications. Grunts and champions receive praise and glory, while peons are often overlooked, though they keep settlements fed and maintained.
Innkeeper Grosk runs the inn in Razor Hill and manages its lodgings and supplies. He offers traveling warriors food, drink, and a hearth, and reminds recruits to rest before facing the wider world.

angles.text: Orcish culture prizes physical might and courage, leaving peons like Ukor at the bottom of the social order. Helping with his delivery shows how humble labor keeps Durotar's fledgling nation working.
You leave the proving grounds for Razor Hill, the center of Horde defense and supplies in southern Durotar.
